identity.name: Chan Santa Cruz
native_names: Noj Kaaj Santa Cruz Xbáalam Naj
alt_names: Maya state of Chan Santa Cruz

land.text: the south-east of the Yucatán peninsula held by the Maya after the Caste War of 1847

predecessors.note: Infobox "Preceded by: Republic of Yucatan"; the Republic had ended in August 1848 (republic-of-yucatan dossier), so the land passed through the Maya rising, not a transfer.

land.text: the state's lands, 'occupied by the Mexican army in 1901'; ceded to Mexico on paper by the British in 1893

successors.note: Infobox "Succeeded by: Mexico". The Territory of Quintana Roo was created by decree on 24 November 1902 (Quintana Roo page); fighting went on at a smaller scale until the war was declared over in September 1915.

capitals.name: Chan Santa Cruz (Noj Kaaj Santa Cruz Xbáalam Naj; today Felipe Carrillo Puerto)
capitals.note: "The capital ... was founded in about 1850 near a sacred cenote"; the state was proclaimed in 1849 in Xocén (not in the gazetteer). Coordinates are those of Felipe Carrillo Puerto.

correction.text: the Maya-held south-east of the peninsula around the shrine of the Talking Cross: 'In 1850, the Maya of the southeast were inspired to continue the struggle'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row. The pages give no extent for the first decade (the infobox map is 'c. 1870'); 120 km around the capital is the researcher's minimal reading and must be treated as soft.

correction.text: 'At its greatest extent, from the 1860s through the 1890s, the Chan Santa Cruz state encompassed all of the southern and central parts' of Quintana Roo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Quintana Roo page gives the modern state as 44,705 km2; the Chan Santa Cruz page gives no area, so the infobox comparison could not be made. The Caste War page has the state 'from north of Tulum to the Belize border and well inland', which would add south-eastern Yucatán and Campeche; those are not drawn. The northern tip (Cancún radius) is left out as the researcher's reading of 'southern and central'.

region.text: the south-east of the peninsula: 'The State of the Cross was proclaimed in 1849 in Xocén'

ledger.note: 1849: the Maya proclaim the State of the Cross at Xocén. 'The State of the Cross was proclaimed in 1849 in Xocén'; infobox 'Established: 1849'. The Caste War page: 'In 1850, the Maya of the southeast were inspired to continue the struggle.' (Reviewer am-08-x, 2026-10-19: counterpart set to federated-republic-of-mexico, since Yucatán had rejoined Mexico on 17 August 1848; region set to the first keyframe's 120 km ring.)

1850: the Maya capital Chan Santa Cruz is founded around the Talking Cross. 'The capital, Noh Kah Balam Nah Chan Santa Cruz, was founded in about 1850 near a sacred cenote.' The page does not name an earlier seat besides Xocén.

region.text: 'all of the southern and central parts' of Quintana Roo at the state's greatest extent

ledger.note: 1860: the state reaches its greatest extent. 'At its greatest extent, from the 1860s through the 1890s, the Chan Santa Cruz state encompassed all of the southern and central parts' of Quintana Roo; the United Kingdom recognized it as a de facto independent nation 'from the late 1850s through 1893'. The page dates the extent to the decade, not a year.

region.text: Chan Santa Cruz and its country, occupied by the Mexican army

ledger.note: May 1901: Mexico occupies Chan Santa Cruz. 'Chan Santa Cruz was occupied by the Mexican army in 1901'; 'Bravo telegraphed the news that the war was over on May 5, 1901' (Caste War page), though fighting continued at a smaller scale.

region.text: the Maya Free State, ended by the Mexican occupation

ledger.note: 1901: the Maya state ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1901'; the 1893 Spenser-Mariscal treaty had already ceded its lands to Mexico on paper and closed British Honduras to its trade; in 1935 General May signed a formal peace treaty with Mexico.

wars.name: Caste War of Yucatán

zones.text: the Maya state's country, southern and central Quintana Roo

wars.outcome: Mexican victory on the ground in 1901: Chan Santa Cruz occupied and the war declared over on 5 May 1901 (and 'officially declared over for the final time in September 1915'); the Maya state had been recognised as de facto independent by Britain from the late 1850s to 1893.
wars.note: The 11 January 1884 treaty signed in Belize City 'recognized Mexican sovereignty over Chan Santa Cruz' and the Chan Santa Cruz page says a treaty was 'never ratified by either party'; neither moved the frontier. The Maya of the Quintana Roo jungle were 'subjugated' in the 1910s according to the Quintana Roo page.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line: the pages give the state's extent only as "the southern and central parts" of Quintana Roo (the infobox map is c. 1870); the 1884 and 1893 treaties did not draw a frontier.

sources.title: Chan Santa Cruz
sources.note: Infobox (1849-1901), capital founded about 1850, extent 1860s-1890s, British recognition to 1893, Mexican occupation 1901, 1935 peace.

sources.title: Caste War of Yucatán
sources.note: Maya rising 30 July 1847, Talking Cross 1850, 1884 Belize City treaty, 5 May 1901, September 1915.

sources.title: Quintana Roo
sources.note: Territory created 24 November 1902; 44,705 km2; Federal Army subdued the Maya in the 1910s; silent on the 1901 occupation and the 1893 treaty.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for the Maya state. Type: state (not rebel): the pages call it a Maya state recognised by Britain as de facto independent for about 35 years; if the colour agent wants hatching for the war years it can be changed to rebel.
The extent is thin: the pages give 'southern and central parts of Quintana Roo' and a c. 1870 map the researcher could not read; the northern tip is cut with a Cancún radius. A gap-filler should open the Spanish 'Estado de Chan Santa Cruz' or the Spenser-Mariscal treaty page for the frontier with Belize and the Hondo river.
Xocén (1849 proclamation) is not in the gazetteer. The 1884 treaty (Belize City, 11 January 1884) is dated by the Caste War page; the Chan Santa Cruz page gives no year for its 'never ratified' treaty, so the two may be one treaty.
The 1860 `gain` names federated-republic-of-mexico as counterpart because the land was Mexican in law; the republic-of-yucatan dossier holds the same land only until August 1848.
